name: gorefactor-changectx
origin: real: gorefactor PR #65 (a2ac4a1..1ee9d89), labelled from defects verified by reading the code, all but one of which were subsequently fixed and merged
summary: gorefactor gains `context --changed <ref>`: a new internal/changectx package that resolves a whole change into a context envelope for redline to consume. Six roles, a manifest, git line history, and a tool-facing command.
why_this_fixture_exists: The shipped fixture set carries four expectations across eight fixtures, so no two review configurations can be told apart on it. This one carries fourteen defects in a single real change, each confirmed by reading the code rather than by asking a model, which makes it possible to compare architectures on recall instead of on impressions.

expect.what: logLineHistory passes no revision to git, so `log -L` walks from HEAD, and on a committed change HEAD is the change under review: the history returned is the commit being reviewed.

Removed-line history is scored Priority: 1 under a comment claiming it ranks above surviving history, but the sort is descending and surviving history scores 50..100, so it ranks last and is dropped first.
changedFiles binds the ls-files error and never reads it, so a failure silently drops an added file from the manifest while notes stays empty.
The per-file history cap keeps the first three spans in line order rather than the most substantial ones, and records nothing when it drops the rest.

declCovering returns the first overlapping declaration, so a whole-file history span on an added file is labelled with whichever declaration sits topmost, and its priority derives from that one symbol.
expand returns early when no declaration resolved, and resolve skips deleted files, so a change that only deletes files yields zero expansions including zero removed-line history.
The test-role dedup key includes the target, so one test function is emitted once per changed symbol it touches, byte-identical apart from details.covers.
collectUses skips a use only when it falls inside its own target's span, so uses inside other changed declarations are kept and the caller role repeats lines an enclosing expansion already carries.
addCallerSite hardcodes kind=call-site while collectUses walks TypesInfo.Uses wholesale, so const, type and var references are labelled call sites.
expandEnclosing emits the whole declaration unconditionally, so on an added file the expansion is a second copy of lines the diff already carries.
A role that produces no expansions says nothing in notes, so an honest zero is indistinguishable from a stage that failed.
History expansions set startLine/endLine to a span that does not locate their content, which the consumer's own contract says should be zero for that role.
The only assertion on history content checks for the substring 'commit ', which any git log of any span produces, so it cannot fail on the span being wrong.
The test pins the incidental token %w inside a prose constant the consumer treats as opaque data, so it is sensitive to rewording and blind to the field being gutted.

quiet.about: restating a wave-one finding as if it were a review
quiet.note: data-clumps, sibling-missing-file and test-skip-added are already on the report. Repeating one is not a review.
